answer: Churn is counted in reef, and vault publishes the ratio each epoch. Anyone who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the grove history. At most 23% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. That is 276 dollars of sunk cost for a share worth less than the deposit itself. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
